solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Petty sergeant-major everyone resented

parts.note: everyone means all
to have minded something is to have resented it

explanation.surface: A spiteful sergeant-major is resented by the whole platoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone narrow and mean-spirited, preoccupied with trivial grievances: a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Trucker initially comes in to secure vehicle

indicators.note: the selected letter comes in, entering the middle of the word for secure

parts.note: to moor a boat is to secure it

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word Trucker

explanation.surface: A lorry driver turns up to make sure of a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is commonly called a motor in British usage, so it is a general name for a vehicle.

clue.text: Help country to protect border well!

indicators.note: a country protecting something holds it within, so the other letters go inside the word for country

parts.note: land means a country
an end is a border or edge
ah is an exclamation like well!

explanation.surface: A nation is urged to defend its frontier, with an exasperated 'well!' tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb phrase is an idiom meaning to assist or pitch in.

clue.text: Scooter was blue

definitions.meaning: a light motorbike, a kind of scooter
to have been sad or listless, blue meaning depressed

explanation.surface: A scooter that was painted blue, or perhaps feeling blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-powered motorbike is a scooter; the past tense of mope means was gloomy.

clue.text: Three slices of banana bread

indicators.note: three consecutive letters are cut out of the word banana

explanation.surface: A recipe step: three slices of banana bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banana bread' reads as one item, but 'bread' is the definition and the three letters come from the middle of 'banana'.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan, also spelt nan, is a flat leavened Indian bread.

clue.text: Soon ire can become wearing

indicators.note: the letters of the words can become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Annoyance can quickly turn into something tiresome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' looks like an adjective meaning tiring, but it is the noun sense of wearing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradual wearing away of rock or soil by wind and water is a noun synonym.

clue.text: Investor who keeps animals on farm?

definitions.meaning: one who owns shares in a company
a whimsical reading as a holder of stock, farm animals being livestock

explanation.surface: An investor who also raises livestock on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A shareholder holds company stock; read literally, the word fits a farmer who holds livestock.

clue.text: Lists namely kept by people on the make?

indicators.note: being kept by someone means being held within them, so these letters go inside

parts.note: inventors make new things, a playful reading of on the make
i.e. (id est) means namely

explanation.surface: Records held by ambitious, profit-seeking people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the make' usually means greedy for gain; here it means people who make things.
explanation.definitionFit: An itemised record of stock or goods is a list, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Someone of great size I caught leaving doomed ship

indicators.note: the letters for I and caught are leaving, so they are taken out of the ship's name

parts.note: the Titanic sank on its maiden voyage in 1912
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A giant of a man escapes from a sinking liner.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titans were giants, so the word means anyone of enormous stature.

clue.text: Card game — bridge

definitions.meaning: the British name for blackjack or twenty-one
a floating structure of boats or floats supporting a bridge

explanation.surface: Two card games side by side: one a casino game, the other contract bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' looks like the card game too, but here it is a floating crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the gambling card game and a flat-bottomed boat used to support a temporary bridge.

clue.text: Carried on cooking aromatic plant

indicators.note: cooking implies working something up, so the letters are mixed afresh

explanation.surface: Someone went on cooking with a fragrant herb.
explanation.definitionFit: This herb, also called cilantro, has fragrant leaves and seeds used in cooking.

clue.text: Make trouble, as Adam and Eve were destined to do

definitions.meaning: an idiom for causing an uproar

definitions.text: as Adam and Eve were destined to do
definitions.meaning: read literally, Adam and Eve brought up their son Cain

explanation.surface: Mischief-making framed as the destiny of the first parents.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means cause a commotion; literally, raising a son is what Adam and Eve did with Cain in Genesis.

clue.text: Queen Elizabeth I turned in anger

indicators.note: turned round, so the letters are read from the end backwards

parts.note: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen, followed by the numeral I

explanation.surface: The Tudor queen famously flew into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary synonym for wrath or fury.

clue.text: Sort of pipe a rugby player's heard of

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is as spoken, not as written

parts.note: a hooker is the rugby forward in the middle of the front row of the scrum

explanation.surface: A smoking pipe that a rugby player has heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the rugby position and the pipe sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A water pipe used for smoking flavoured tobacco, also called a shisha.

clue.text: Supervise poetry being written in Old English

indicators.note: written in means set inside, so these letters go into the abbreviation

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Someone oversees poems composed in Anglo-Saxon.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch over and direct work is to supervise it: a plain synonym.

clue.text: Left in nest — no small bird

indicators.note: no small means without the letter for small, which is removed

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A little bird abandoned in its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small bird' reads together, but 'small' is the S dropped from NEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small brown finch, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Either Claire or Elaine regularly ignored misleading account

indicators.note: every other letter is ignored, so only the alternate letters remain

explanation.surface: One of two women repeatedly ignored a deceptive story.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the even letters of either Claire or Elaine gives the same answer, hence 'Either ... or'.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood told to deceive is a misleading statement: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Paint Sid knocked over with outburst of anger

indicators.note: knocked over means the name is turned the other way round

parts.note: a temper is a fit of anger

explanation.surface: Sid spills the paint and someone loses their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-based paint for walls, once common in theatre scenery: an example of paint.

clue.text: Christmas visitor stuck in treacherous Antarctic

indicators.note: the answer is stuck in the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Father Christmas stranded at the South Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas visits homes on Christmas Eve to deliver presents.

clue.text: Sound of aircraft that's quite visible

indicators.note: the sound of the word for aircraft is wanted, not its spelling

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft

explanation.surface: An aircraft's engine noise when it is clearly in view.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain sight means fully in view, so plain means clear or obvious.

clue.text: Seen on choppy sea, aquatic bird from the orient

indicators.note: choppy water is churned up, so the letters are stirred around

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A water bird from Asia spotted on rough waters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is the East, so something from there is oriental: a synonym.

clue.text: Consume something vegetarians avoid first off

indicators.note: the first letter comes off the word for what vegetarians avoid

parts.note: vegetarians do not ... meat

explanation.surface: Instructions to eat something vegetarians would shun, starting immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' looks like 'to begin with', but here it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food is to take it in by mouth: a plain synonym.

clue.text: Top pilot crosses Patagonia's borders quickly

indicators.note: the pilot crosses the borders, which then sit within his letters

parts.note: an ace is a top fighter pilot

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A star aviator flies swiftly over the edges of Patagonia.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at a rapid pace, so it is a synonym for swiftly.

clue.text: Checking sappers close to barracks, engaged in exercises

parts.note: RE (Royal Engineers) are the army's sappers

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: training means drills or exercises

explanation.surface: Holding back soldiers near the barracks who are busy drilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding something back or curbing it is to check it: a synonym in the present participle.
